business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business section (P1).
business_model.claim: The company's customers fall into three broad groups: transient business (individual business or leisure travelers, with business travelers historically the majority of transient demand), group business (clusters of 10+ rooms booked together), and contract business (blocks of rooms sold to a specific company at discounted rates for extended periods).
quotes: Transient business broadly represents individual business or leisure travelers. Historically, business travelers have made up the majority of transient demand at our hotels.
Group business represents clusters of guestrooms booked together, usually with a minimum of 10 rooms.
Contract business refers to blocks of rooms sold to a specific company for an extended period of time at significantly discounted rates.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K MD&A (P3); Q3 2026 stats from the 8-K earnings release (P5).
business_model.claim: Occupancy and average daily rate (ADR) are the primary drivers of rooms revenue; occupancy and the type of customer are the primary drivers of food and beverage revenue; occupancy and the nature of on-property amenities drive other revenue.
quotes: Occupancy and ADR are the major drivers of rooms revenues.
Occupancy and the type of customer staying at the hotel are the major drivers of food and beverage revenue
Occupancy and the nature of amenities at the property are the main drivers of other revenue.

business_model.claim: Most variable operating expenses, including housekeeping labor, fluctuate with occupancy, while increases in ADR raise only limited cost categories (management and franchise fees based on revenue), so ADR growth has a more significant impact on operating margins than occupancy growth.
quotes: Most categories of variable operating expenses, including labor costs such as housekeeping, fluctuate with changes in occupancy. Increases in occupancy are accompanied by increases in most categories of variable operating expenses, while increases in ADR typically only result in increases in limited categories of operating costs and expenses, such as management fees and franchise fees, which are based on hotel revenues. Thus, changes in ADR have a more significant impact on operating margins than changes in occupancy.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K MD&A (P3) and 10-Q MD&A (P4).
business_model.claim: Third-party hotel management companies earn base management fees as a percentage of gross revenue and incentive management fees as a percentage of net operating income above a threshold; franchise fees are computed as a percentage of rooms revenues.
quotes: Base management fees are computed as a percentage of gross revenue. Management fees also include incentive management fees, which are typically a percentage of net operating income (or similar measurements of hotel profitability) above an annual threshold. Franchise fees are computed as a percentage of rooms revenues.
The management companies typically earn base and incentive management fees based on the levels of revenues and profitability of each individual hotel.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Risk Factors (P2) and 10-K MD&A (P3).
business_model.claim: Many real estate costs and certain hotel operating costs (real estate taxes, insurance premiums, maintenance, utilities) are fixed and do not decrease when revenue falls, making profits more sensitive to revenue declines than to revenue increases.
quotes: Many real estate costs and certain hotel operating costs are fixed, even if revenue from our hotels decreases.

These expenses include certain personnel costs, rent, property taxes, insurance and utilities, as well as sales and marketing expenses. If we are unable to decrease these costs significantly or rapidly when demand for our hotels decreases, the resulting decline in our revenues can have an adverse effect on our net cash flow, margins and profits.
